_qa.public_tldr: This collection of 1946–1947 internal military correspondence includes the famous Twining Memo, in which Air Materiel Command formally assessed that flying disc sightings represented something real — not hallucinations or fiction. The documents trace how the military ruled out domestic US projects as the source, investigated foreign origins including captured German aircraft designs, and ultimately established the first official Air Force UFO investigation program.

It includes a specific sighting report from Hobson, Ohio, references to German Horten Brothers flying wing designs being evaluated in connection with the phenomenon, and records the Air Force's rejection of a proposal to keep fighter jets on continuous alert to chase the objects.

_qa.public_headline: French Military Officials Urged Governments to Take UFOs Seriously in 1999 Report
_qa.public_tldr: This document is the English translation of the COMETA Report, a 1999 study by retired French military and civilian officials examining well-documented UFO cases from multiple countries. Accompanied by a cover letter from Carol Rosin (former spokesperson for Wernher von Braun) to a NASA contact, the report recommended that authorities treat UFO phenomena seriously, including considering the extraterrestrial hypothesis and its defence implications.

name: 255_t_763_r1b_transcripts.pdf
title: NASA-UAP-D3, Gemini 7 Transcript, 1965
description:
Gemini 7 was the tenth crewed American spaceflight. This document is a transcript of communications between the flight crew, Astronauts James “Jim” Lovell and Frank Borman, and the Manned Flight Center (now known as Johnson Space Center) in Houston, Texas. The transcript begins with Borman’s report of a “bogey,” contemporary nomenclature for an unknown aircraft, as well as a debris field. Borman described the debris field as consisting of “very, very many […] hundreds of little particles.” He estimated the particles’ distance from the spacecraft to be four miles. Lovell described observing a “brilliant body in the sun against a black background with trillions of particles on it.”
This document also includes handwritten notes documenting the encounter, annotated with the phrase “UFO Sighting by Borman” in the top right corner.

_qa.public_headline: Gemini 7 Crew Reported Unidentified Object and Debris Field in Orbit, 1965
_qa.public_tldr: This 1965 NASA transcript records Gemini 7 astronauts Frank Borman and Jim Lovell reporting an unidentified "bogey" and a large field of small particles while in low Earth orbit, distinct from their own mission's booster. Houston Mission Control acknowledged the sighting but never provided an explanation in the transcript.

_qa.public_tldr: This collection of U.S. and British military cables from early 1945 documents repeated encounters by the 415th Night Fighter Squadron with unexplained lights — nicknamed 'foofighters' — that followed Allied aircraft over Germany. A separate incident involved an unidentified cylindrical object attacked at 9,000 feet. The British Air Ministry acknowledged the phenomena remained 'something of a mystery' with no definitive explanation.

The reports typically include information such as dates, locations, weather, and altitude, plus detailed descriptions of appearance and movement. Some messages from the Military Air Transport Service (MATS) and Army Airways Communications System (AACS) are also included, as well as additional military intelligence reports, several diagrams, and a report from a weather station in Japan.

Witnesses included military personnel, civilian pilots, and air traffic controllers who described objects ranging from spherical lights to delta-wing formations, with only one sighting conclusively explained as a weather balloon.

name: nasa-uap-d1-apollo-12-transcript-1969.pdf
title: NASA-UAP-D1, Apollo 12 Transcript, 1969
description:
Apollo 12 was the fourth crewed U.S. mission to the Moon and the second to land astronauts on the lunar surface. This document is an excerpt from the Apollo 12 Technical Air-to-Ground Voice Transcription, November 1969, highlighting two periods in which astronauts reported observing unidentified phenomenon: a one hour period on the fifth day, and a two minute period on the sixth day. These transcripts contain contemporaneous observations by the flight crew reacting to unidentified phenomenon.
•	Day 05, Hour 19, Minute 14, Second 58 through Day 05, Hour 20, Minute 12, Second 14:
o	At 05:19:27:25, the pilot of the Lunar Module (LMP-LM), Astronaut Alan L. Bean, described observing particles and flashes of light “sailing off in space” via the onboard Alignment Optical Telescope (AOT). He characterized these phenomenon as “escaping the Moon.”
•	Day 06, Hour 00, Minute 21, Second 42 through Day 06, Hour 00, Minute 23, Second 33:
o	Mission Commander, Charles “Pete” Conrad, described observing floating debris outside the lunar module, which had been illuminated by the module’s onboard tracking light. At 06:00:21:51, Conrad assessed that the tracking light had burnt out because he could no longer see the debris from the module.

_qa.public_headline: Apollo 12 Crew Reported Unexplained Lights and Debris Near the Moon
_qa.public_tldr: This document is an excerpt from the Apollo 12 air-to-ground voice transcript from November 1969, in which astronauts reported seeing fast-moving particles of light near the Moon and small debris floating alongside their spacecraft. Houston Mission Control offered prosaic explanations for most observations, including water droplets and electromagnetic interference, though some details — like particles that appeared to be 'escaping the Moon' — were not fully resolved in the transcript.

name: nasa-uap-d2-apollo-17-transcript-1972.pdf
title: NASA-UAP-D2, Apollo 17 Transcript, 1972
description:
Apollo 17 was the ninth crewed U.S. mission to the Moon, and the sixth to land astronauts on the lunar surface. This document is an excerpt from the Apollo 17 Technical Air-to-Ground Voice Transcription, December 1972, highlighting three periods in which astronauts reported observing unidentified phenomenon: a nine minute period on the first day, a three hour period on the second day, and a six minute period on the third day. 
•	Day 00, Hour 03, Minute 34, Second 10 through Day 00, Hour 03, Minute 42, Second 29:
    o	Command Module Pilot (CMP), Ronald Evans, reported observing “very bright particles or fragments” drifting and “tumbling” near the spacecraft as it maneuvered. Lunar Module Pilot (LMP), Harrison “Jack” Schmitt, described the phenomenon as looking “like the Fourth of July.” The astronauts speculated that the phenomenon may be attributable to ice or paint fragments dislodging from a separated component of the spacecraft (S-IVB) but characterized that assessment as a “wild guess.”
•	Day 02, Hour 18, Minute 42, Second 34 through Day 02, Hour 21, Minute 07, Second 05:
    o	Mission Commander, Eugene A. Cernan, reported difficulty sleeping and described having observed “some sets of the streaks.” He also described an intense light flashing between his eyes, describing its intensity as comparable to that of a train headlight and characterizing it as “imposing.” Over the next three hours, Cernan described observing several flashing, rotating phenomenon that he assessed as corresponding to physical objects in space rather than a purely optical phenomenon. LMP Schmitt also reported observing similar phenomenon, though he again assessed the source of his observation to be a separated rocket stage (S-IVB). At 02:20:55:22, Cernan reported observing two additional distant flashing objects, though he assessed them as Spacecraft/Lunar Module Adapter panels (SLA panel), another separated component of the Saturn V rocket.
•	Day 03, Hour 15, Minute 33, Second 25 through Day 03, Hour 15, Minute 39, Second 46:
    o	At 03:15:38:09, LMP Schmitt exclaimed that he had observed a flash on the lunar surface north of Grimaldi (crater).

_qa.public_headline: Apollo 17 Astronauts Reported Bright Objects Near Spacecraft in 1972
_qa.public_tldr: This document is an excerpt from the Apollo 17 mission's air-to-ground radio transcript from 1972, highlighting moments when astronauts reported seeing bright particles, a distant flashing object, and a flash on the lunar surface. The crew themselves proposed ordinary explanations for most observations — spacecraft debris, ice, peeling paint, or a meteorite impact — and none were treated as unexplained by the crew or Mission Control.

name: nasa-uap-d4-apollo-11-technical-crew-debriefing-1969.pdf
title: NASA-UAP-D4, Apollo 11 Technical Crew Debriefing, 1969
description:
Apollo 11 was the third crewed mission to the Moon and the first to land Astronauts on the lunar surface. This document is an excerpt from the Apollo 11 Technical Crew Debriefing (Volumes 1 and 2) from July 31, 1969. The document highlights three observations: one, an object on the way out to the Moon; two, flashes of light inside the cabin; and three, a sighting on the return trip of a bright light tentatively assumed by the crew to be a laser.

•	Page 6-33 (Vol. 1). [Lunar Module Pilot for Apollo 11, Buzz Aldrin]: “The first unusual thing that we saw I guess was 1 day out or something pretty close to the moon. It had a sizeable dimension to it, so we put the monocular on it.” The crew speculated that it could have been the S-IVB stage of the Saturn V launch vehicle.
•	Page 6-37 (Vol. 1). [Lunar Module Pilot for Apollo 11, Buzz Aldrin] “The other observation that I made accumulated gradually. I don’t know whether I saw it the first night, but I’m sure I saw it the second night. I was trying to go to sleep with all the lights out. I observed what I thought were little flashes inside the cabin, spaced a couple of minutes apart…”
•	Page 21-1 (Vol. 2). [Lunar Module Pilot for Apollo 11, Buzz Aldrin] “I observed what appeared to be a fairly bright light source which we tentatively ascribed to a possible laser.”

_qa.public_headline: Apollo 11 Crew Reported Three Unusual Sightings During Moon Mission
_qa.public_tldr: A originally-classified NASA debriefing from July 31, 1969 records the Apollo 11 crew describing three unexplained observations during their mission: an L-shaped object seen en route to the Moon, repeated light flashes inside the darkened cabin, and a bright light from lunar orbit later attributed to sunlight reflecting off water. The crew offered no definitive explanations and in some cases suspected mundane origins.

name: nasa-uap-d5-apollo-17-crew-debriefing-for-science-1973.pdf
title: NASA-UAP-D5, Apollo 17 Crew Debriefing for Science, 1973
description:
Apollo 17 was the ninth crewed U.S. mission to the Moon, and the sixth to land Astronauts on the lunar surface. This document is an excerpt from the Apollo 17 Crew Debriefing for Science on January 8, 1973, in which Dick Henry, co-investigator on the ultraviolet experiment on Apollo 17, discusses seeing results that were unexpected. 
•	Pages 119-120. “One of the most exciting results of X-ray astronomy was the fact that an X-ray background was observed over the sky that nobody had expected, and part of this is the gamma-ray background that Dr. Trombka talked about. In the UV, nobody knows, but you never know until you look. You do have to deal with this background of stars that we know is there. So, we did look at a large number of different points at high galactic latitudes, both north and south. The spectrum that we see is above this dark count. In other words, this abnormally high dark current did not, in fact, interfere with that experiment. The spectrum that we see looks like the spectrum of the hot star; however, we know that there were no hot stars within our field of view. Therefore, the most conservative interpretation, I think, is that what we're seeing is light from hot stars in the galactic plane going up out of the plane and reflecting off interstellar dust. There are certain characteristics of the spectrum, though, that don't fit that theory, and it's at least possible that this is extragalactic radiation. I'm looking forward very much to the detailed computer study of this, but it's going to take a long time.”

_qa.public_headline: Apollo 17 Science Debrief Recorded Unexplained UV and X-Ray Observations
_qa.public_tldr: This is an excerpt from NASA's Apollo 17 crew science debriefing, dated January 8, 1973. The transcript records scientists discussing unexpected ultraviolet and X-ray observations made during the mission, including a UV spectrum that resembled a hot star where no hot stars existed, and an unexplained X-ray background across the sky. These are astrophysics findings, not reports of unidentified craft.

name: nasa-uap-d6-apollo-17-technical-crew-debriefing-1973.pdf
title: NASA-UAP-D6, Apollo 17 Technical Crew Debriefing, 1973
description:
Apollo 17 was the ninth crewed U.S. mission to the Moon, and the sixth to land Astronauts on the lunar surface. This document is an excerpt from the Apollo 17 Technical Crew Debriefing on January 4, 1973, in which astronaut Harrison Schmitt reported seeing light flashes.
•	Page 24-4. [Lunar Module Pilot Harrison Schmitt]: “We had light flashes just about continuously during the whole flight when we were dark adapted. I had one which I thought was a flash on the lunar surface. That one period of time when we had the blindfolds on for the ALFMED [Apollo Light Flash Moving Emulsion Detector] experiment there were just no visible flashes, although that evening, that night, before I went to sleep, I noticed that I was seeing the light flashes again.”

_qa.public_headline: Apollo 17 Crew Reported Continuous Light Flashes During 1973 Moon Mission
_qa.public_tldr: This is a two-page excerpt from the Apollo 17 Technical Crew Debriefing, dated January 4, 1973, in which astronauts describe seeing nearly continuous light flashes throughout the flight when their eyes were dark-adapted. The flashes — a phenomenon already under scientific study via an onboard experiment — temporarily stopped during a blindfold test, then resumed, and one crew member believed he saw a flash on the lunar surface itself.

name: nasa-uap-d7-skylab-technical-crew-debriefing-1973.pdf
title: NASA-UAP-D7, Skylab Techincal Crew Debriefing 1973
description:
Launched on May 14, 1973, Skylab was the United States’ first laboratory in space. From 1973 to 1974, the station was visited by three crews. This document contains excerpts from all three crews to visit the station. In the first excerpt taken from Skylab 1/2 [first crew] Technical Debriefing from June 30, 1973, highlights crew observations of light flashes. The second excerpt taken from Skylab 1/3 Technical Crew Debriefing from October 4, 1973, highlights two observations—a satellite in similar orbit and another object with a “reddish hue to it.” The final excerpt taken from the Skylab 1/4 Technical Crew Debriefing from February 22, 1974, highlights an observation of flashing lights outside Skylab.
•	Skylab 2 crew observation: 
o	Page 23-20. [Science Pilot for Skylab 2, Joesph Kerwin] “We saw light flashes. I think all of us saw them. I saw them most often when I was in the sack at night with my eyes closed but awake naturally. They tended to wax and wane in frequency.”
•	Skylab 3 crew observations: 
o	Page 7-4. [Science Pilot for Skylab 3, Owen Garriott] “We saw that satellite about a week before splashdown. That was one of the most unusual things that we saw and I guess Jack [Lousma] noticed it looking out the window. This bright reddish object was out there and we tracked it for about 5 or 10 minutes. It was obviously a satellite in a very similar orbit to our own.”
o	Page 20-1. [Science Pilot for Skylab 3, Owen Garriott] “Jack [Lousma] first noticed this rather large red star out the wardroom window. Upon close examination, it was much brighter than Jupiter or any of the other planets. It had a reddish hue to it, even though it was well above the horizon.”
•	Skylab 4 crew observation 
o	Page 7-8. [Commander for Skylab 4, Gerald P. Carr] “One other area of unusual events that we reported on the dump tapes was that on occasion we saw some lights flashing outside with very a definite motion relative to ours. We presumed that they were other pieces of Skylab, or possibly other satellites.”

_qa.public_headline: Skylab Astronauts Reported Unexplained Lights and an Unidentified Object in Orbit
_qa.public_tldr: This NASA document compiles excerpts from crew debriefings after all three Skylab missions (1973–1974), in which astronauts described light flashes, an unidentified bright reddish object tracked for about 10 minutes, and flashing lights moving outside the station. The most notable observation — a rotating reddish object in a similar orbit — was never identified by NASA despite the crew's request for an explanation.

name: dos-uap-d1-cable-1-papua-new-guinea-january-1985.pdf
title: State Department UAP Cable 1, Papua New Guinea, January 28, 1985
description:
This document is a U.S. Department of State diplomatic cable from the U.S. Embassy in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea to USCINCPAC (United States Indo-Pacific Command) at Honolulu, HI on January 28, 1985. 
The cable reports that the U.S. Embassy to Papua New Guinea received an inquiry from the host nation’s intelligence services regarding reports of high-altitude, high-speed aircraft in Papua New Guinean airspace on the evening of January 24, 1985. The cable refers to a representative of the local intelligence services as “NIO,” or National Intelligence Officer, throughout. The NIO relayed to U.S. diplomatic personnel that residents had been “frightened by overflights, which led to the provincial premier’s calling of a public meeting on the subject.” The NIO also stated there had been “various reports of unidentified aerial phenomena the night of January 24, including fast-moving objects with lights, contrails, and noise.” The NIO assessed these reports as credible based upon the testimony of an Air Niugini pilot who said that their radar had “picked up aircraft flying south to north at high altitude and high speed.”
The cable concludes by characterizing the information provided by the NIO as “very sketchy.” It also sought clarification from U.S. INDOPACOM on the presence or absence of U.S. military aircraft within Papua New Guinean airspace on the night in question.

_qa.public_headline: U.S. Embassy reported unidentified high-speed aircraft over Papua New Guinea in 1985
_qa.public_tldr: A 1985 U.S. State Department cable from the Embassy in Port Moresby reported that Papua New Guinea's intelligence agency asked about unidentified high-altitude, high-speed aircraft seen over the country on the evening of January 24, 1985. The Embassy denied any knowledge of U.S. aircraft in PNG airspace that night and asked U.S. Pacific Command for confirmation.

name: dos-uap-d2-cable-2-kazakhstan-january-1994.pdf
title: State Department UAP Cable 2, Kazakhstan, January 31, 1994
description:
This document is a U.S. Department of State diplomatic cable from the U.S. Embassy in Dushanbe, Tajikistan to the Secretary of State in Washington, D.C. on January 31, 1994.
On January 27, 1994 one Tajik pilot and three American citizens encountered an UAP flying a 747 jet at 41,000 feet over Kazakhstan.  Object was a bright light of enormous intensity and approached over the horizon to the east at great speed and a much higher altitude.  Several pictures were taken of the craft making 90 degree turns, doing corkscrews and maneuvering in circles a great rates of speed.  Object was reported as resembling a bullet in flight.  Visual estimation of the contrails were at 100,000 feet, which was too high to leave contrails by ordinary aircraft.

_qa.public_headline: U.S. Embassy Cable Reports Pilot UFO Encounter Over Kazakhstan in 1994
_qa.public_tldr: A January 1994 U.S. State Department cable from the embassy in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, relays an American airline pilot's account of observing an unidentified object performing unusual maneuvers at extreme altitude over Kazakhstan. The embassy explicitly stated it had no opinion on the sighting and passed the report along without endorsement.

name: 059uap00011.pdf
title: State Department UAP Cable 3, Tbilisi, Georgia, October 30, 2001
description: On October 28-29, there was an incident alleged by the Georgian Foreign Ministry that Russian aircraft had violated Georgian airspace and bombed areas of the Kodori Gorge.  Russians denied any of the claims and said that it could have been UFOs.  Cable authors note that Russians typically engage in the “bold lie” when they wish to conceal actions.

_qa.public_headline: Russian Official Dismissed Georgian Airspace Reports as 'UFOs' in 2001 Diplomatic Cable
_qa.public_tldr: A 2001 U.S. State Department cable from the American Embassy in Moscow documents Russian officials categorically denying that Russian planes bombed Georgia's Kodori Gorge, with one official sarcastically suggesting the reported aircraft could have been 'UFOs.' The document is not a UFO sighting report — it records a diplomatic exchange about alleged military airspace violations and Russian troop withdrawal from a base in Abkhazia.

name: 059uap00012.pdf
title: State Department UAP Cable 4, Ashgabat, Turkmenistan, November 5, 2004
description: UFOlogists of Turkmenistan has gained a positive reputation as a reliable partner for the United States in Turkmenistan to the bemusement of the cable’s author in the build up of civil society organizations within the country.  The reputation has become earned because everyone in Turkmenistan, apparently, “is interested in UFOs.”

_qa.public_headline: U.S. Embassy Cable Profiles Turkmen UFO Group Turned NGO Partner
_qa.public_tldr: A November 2004 unclassified cable from the U.S. Embassy in Ashgabat describes how the Union of UFOlogists of Turkmenabat — originally founded to study extraterrestrial life — became one of America's most reliable civil society partners in Turkmenistan. The cable is not about a UFO sighting; it documents an NGO that used universal local interest in UFOs to maintain good relations with authorities while doing development work.

name: 059uap00013.pdf
title: State Department UAP Cable 5, Mexico, September 16, 2003
description: On September 12, 20023 the Mexican Congress heard testimony on UAP from experts related to the debate about an Aerial Space Protection Law, which, if approved, would make Mexico the first country to formally acknowledge the presence of alien life on earth. Experts asked legislators to recognize UAP, guarantee airspace security, and allow UAP to be studied.  They presented to alleged alien corpses and videos of Mexican pilot’s encounters with fast-moving flying objects during flight. Disagreement about the efficacy and validity of the purported alien corpses.

_qa.public_headline: U.S. Embassy Cable Reported Mexico's 2023 Congressional UAP Hearing
_qa.public_tldr: A routine weekly political briefing cable from the U.S. Embassy in Mexico reported on a September 12, 2023 Mexican congressional hearing about unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP), during which alleged alien corpses were presented alongside pilot encounter videos. The cable noted that a key witness, former U.S. Navy pilot Ryan Graves, publicly condemned the corpse display as an "unsubstantiated stunt," and that scientists had previously discredited similar specimens from the same presenter.

name: usper-statement-redacted.pdf
title: USPER Statement about UAP Sighting
description: This is an FBI 302 interview conducted with a senior US intelligence official regarding his first-hand account of a UAP encounter at a US military facility. USPER relayed to FBI agents that he and other federal and state personnel conducted searches to where orbs had been previously seen.  After searching the area with a helicopter, they found a “super-hot” orb hovering over the ground.  The orb is reported to have travelled for 20 miles at a speed too fast for the helicopter in pursuit.  An additional “swarm” of lights were seen moving in all directions.  A total of four or five additional orbs were seen shortly thereafter for a short time, flaring up and then down.  This pattern of four or five orbs flaring up, then down continued over the next thirty minutes across the area.

_qa.public_headline: FBI Document Records Intelligence Official's Account of Multiple Orb Encounters
_qa.public_tldr: A SECRET//NOFORN FBI interview summary describes a senior US intelligence official's first-hand account of encountering numerous unidentified orbs during a helicopter search mission at a US military facility in late 2025. The objects displayed behaviors including splitting apart, forming patterns, swarming, and outpacing a pursuing helicopter — but the document is so heavily redacted that names, dates, locations, and facility details are all blacked out.

name: 2024-04-30-composite-sketch.pdf
title: FBI September 2023 Sighting - Composite Sketch
description: Actual site photo with FBI Lab rendered graphic overlay depicting corroborating eyewitness reports from September 2023 of an apparent ellipsoid bronze metallic object materializing out of a bright light in the sky, 130-195 feet in length, and disappearing instantaneously.

title: FBI September 2023 Sighting - Serial 3
description: This is an FBI 302 interview conducted with a US citizen regarding their first-hand account of a UAP encounter at a US test site.  USPER described an object "metallic bronze in color."

_qa.public_headline: FBI Interview Records Witness Account of Unexplained Light in 2023
_qa.public_tldr: This is page 2 of a two-page FBI witness interview form (FD-302) documenting a UAP sighting in September 2023. The witness initially thought the light was a meteor burning up in the atmosphere, but the document is so heavily redacted that most details — including the witness's name, exact date, and location — are obscured.

title: FBI September 2023 Sighting - Serial 4
description: This is an FBI 302 interview conducted with a US citizen regarding their first-hand account of a UAP encounter at a US test site. USPER described an object "metallic/gray in color."

_qa.public_headline: FBI Documents Government Employee's Silent Cigar-Shaped Object Over Military Base
_qa.public_tldr: An FBI interview report from September 2023 records a US government employee describing a large, silent, cigar-shaped object hovering over a military test site. The object, described as metallic bronze with an intense white light, was also seen by a second witness before it vanished within seconds.

name: serial-4-redacted_redacted.pdf
title: FBI September 2023 Sighting - Serial 5
description: This is an FBI 302 interview conducted with a US citizen regarding their first-hand account of a UAP encounter at a US test site. USPER described a "bright light over the horizon."

_qa.public_headline: FBI Interview Records UAP Sighting at US Test Site
_qa.public_tldr: This FBI witness interview report (FD-302 form) documents a first-hand account of an unidentified aerial phenomenon seen at a US test site in September 2023. The witness described an object of constant size and light intensity in airspace that had been restricted for drone testing, and reported disturbed sleep and unusual dreams in the days that followed.

name: western_us_event_slides_5.08.2026.pdf
title: Western US Event
description: This document is a summary of statements by seven US PERSONs employed by the federal government who separately reported observing several unidentified anomalous phenomena in the western United States over the course of two days in 2023.  The summary notes the US PERSONS reported four distinct categories of experiences, including observing “orbs launching other orbs” at a distance, observing a large stationary glowing orb at close estimated range, pursuing a large phenomenon near the ground, and observing a large, seemingly transparent phenomenon, reported to being akin to a “translucent kite.” Although there is no technical data directly associated with this report, contextual factors — such as these events sharing features with others reported to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), the reporters’ credibility, and the potentially anomalous nature of the events themselves — combine to make this report among the most compelling within AARO’s current holdings.

_qa.public_headline: Seven Federal Agents Reported Multiple Unidentified Objects Over Western US
_qa.public_tldr: A Department of War briefing summarizes witness statements from seven federal law enforcement agents who observed several distinct unidentified phenomena — glowing orbs, a triangular "kite," and a semi-transparent object — over two days in 2023 in a restricted area of the western United States. The report is based entirely on witness testimony with no sensor data or technical analysis included.

_qa.public_headline: Gemini 7 Crew Reported Unidentified Object and Particles in 1965 Orbit
_qa.public_tldr: This is an audio excerpt from NASA's Gemini 7 mission in 1965, replayed by Houston mission control, in which the crew reported seeing an unidentified object and small particles during their second orbit near Antigua. The object, referred to as a "bogey," was distinct from the spacecraft's own booster and nearby particles.

_qa.public_headline: U.S. Agency Concludes Iraq Air Base Object Was Likely Balloons
_qa.public_tldr: The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) investigated an unidentified object recorded on infrared video at Al Taqaddum Air Base, Iraq, in October 2017. The agency concluded with high confidence that the object was a cluster of balloons and showed no anomalous behavior.

description: AARO document mirrored from aaro.mil. Original URL: https://www.aaro.mil/Portals/136/PDFs/case_resolution_reports/Mt-Etna-Object.pdf

_qa.public_headline: Military Drone Filmed Mystery Object Near Mt. Etna; Agency Says Balloon
_qa.public_tldr: A 2025 report from the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) analyzes infrared video from a U.S. military drone that captured a round object apparently flying at high speed near Mt. Etna, Italy in December 2018. AARO concluded with moderate confidence that the object was a small balloon moving at wind speed, and that its seemingly extraordinary behavior was an optical illusion caused by the drone's own movement.

title: AARO Puerto Rico UAP Case Resolution
description: AARO document mirrored from aaro.mil. Original URL: https://www.aaro.mil/Portals/136/PDFs/case_resolution_reports/AARO_Puerto_Rico_UAP_Case_Resolution.pdf

_qa.public_headline: Pentagon Office Attributes 2013 Puerto Rico UAP Sighting to Sky Lanterns
_qa.public_tldr: A March 2025 report by the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) concludes that a widely discussed 2013 infrared video of unidentified objects near Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, most likely captured a pair of sky lanterns drifting in the wind — not an anomalous craft. AARO found the objects moved at roughly 8 mph (matching wind speed), never entered the water, and appeared to vanish only because the infrared camera lost thermal contrast against the ocean.

_qa.public_headline: Pentagon Office Concludes GoFast UFO Video Shows No Extraordinary Flight
_qa.public_tldr: The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) analyzed the well-known 'Go Fast' Navy infrared video from January 2015 and concluded with high confidence that the object did not demonstrate anomalous speed or performance. The object's apparent velocity was an optical illusion caused by the fast-moving jet, and the object was likely a small drone or bird-sized object drifting roughly with the wind at 13,000 feet.

name: Case_Resolution_of_Atmospheric_Wakes_508-02262024.pdf
title: Case Resolution Of Atmospheric Wakes 508 02262024
description: AARO document mirrored from aaro.mil. Original URL: https://www.aaro.mil/Portals/136/PDFs/case_resolution_reports/Case_Resolution_of_Atmospheric_Wakes_508-02262024.pdf

_qa.public_headline: Pentagon Office Explains Mysterious UFO Wakes as Camera Artifacts
_qa.public_tldr: The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), a Pentagon unit, reviewed three UAP (unidentified anomalous phenomena) cases from the Middle East and Mediterranean Sea where drone operators recorded objects with apparent atmospheric wakes on infrared cameras. AARO concluded with high confidence that the wakes were sensor artifacts caused by objects moving quickly across the camera's field of view, not signs of unusual propulsion. The objects themselves were identified as ordinary aircraft, including a military plane and an Airbus A380 airliner.

_qa.public_headline: Military Pilot's UAP Near Eglin Base Resolved as Likely Balloon
_qa.public_tldr: AARO (All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office) investigated a January 2023 sighting of an unidentified object near Eglin Air Force Base, Florida, where a military pilot detected four objects on radar and visually observed one. The agency and two independent partners concluded with moderate-to-high confidence that the object was most likely a commercial lighting balloon, with no anomalous characteristics.

_qa.public_headline: Pentagon Office Identified Southeast Asia Triangle UAP as Fishing Nets
_qa.public_tldr: The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) resolved a UAP case involving six dark triangular objects spotted in 2017 satellite imagery over Southeast Asia. The agency concluded with high confidence that the objects were cone-shaped fishing nets floating on the ocean surface, based on size analysis, newer imagery from 2023, and stock footage of nets on the same river.

_qa.public_headline: AARO Resolved Western US UAP Sighting as Distant Commercial Aircraft
_qa.public_tldr: This is a case resolution report from the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) investigating a 2021 UAP sighting in the Western United States. Military personnel reported five equidistant lights in restricted airspace, but AARO concluded they were almost certainly commercial aircraft up to 300 nautical miles away, with apparent shape changes caused by sensor vibration and autofocus issues.

name: 2025_UAP_Workshop_Paper.pdf
title: 2025 UAP Workshop Paper
description: AARO document mirrored from aaro.mil. Original URL: https://www.aaro.mil/Portals/136/PDFs/Information%20Papers/2025_UAP_Workshop_Paper.pdf

_qa.public_headline: AARO Workshop Tackled How to Collect and Analyze UAP Reports
_qa.public_tldr: In August 2025, the Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) sponsored a two-day workshop in Washington, DC, bringing together 40 participants from government, academia, and independent research to address problems with collecting, organizing, and analyzing UAP reports. The workshop focused entirely on data methodology — not on what UAPs are — and concluded that most reports are fragmented and unstructured, that AI tools carry serious risks of bias, and that classification and stigma remain major barriers to better data.

_qa.public_headline: Proposed DHS Program to Study Non-Human Materials Was Rejected and Never Operated
_qa.public_tldr: KONA BLUE was a proposed Department of Homeland Security special access program intended to investigate "non-human biologics" and advanced aerospace vehicles, building on earlier Pentagon-funded research. It was shut down six months after being proposed in 2011 due to inadequate justification, and no materials, data, or funding were ever transferred to it.

_qa.public_headline: DHS Released All Records on Terminated Program KONA BLUE to Defense Department
_qa.public_tldr: In February 2024, the Department of Homeland Security declassified and released all documents related to KONA BLUE, a prospective special access program it had terminated in 2012. The accompanying material includes justifications for restricting a related Pentagon program called AATIP, citing concerns about exotic technologies that could be weaponised by adversaries.

_qa.public_tldr: Oak Ridge National Laboratory analyzed a metallic specimen claimed to be connected to a UAP event over central Ohio in the mid-1990s. Using multiple chemical and radiological techniques, the lab concluded the material is a conventional aluminum-silicon casting alloy matching standard industrial grades, with no anomalous properties detected.

_qa.public_headline: AARO Lab Analysis Finds Ohio UAP-Linked Metal Is Ordinary Aluminum
_qa.public_tldr: A January 2026 supplement from the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) reports that a metallic specimen allegedly linked to a UAP sighting near Flint Ridge State Park, Ohio, was analyzed by Oak Ridge National Laboratory and found to be an ordinary aluminum alloy with no unusual properties. AARO concludes the material most likely came from conventional industrial or commercial sources.

_qa.public_headline: AARO Explains Why Most UAP Data Stays Classified
_qa.public_tldr: This September 2025 information paper from the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) explains why UAP-related data is typically classified — to protect military sensors and methods, not the UAP subject matter itself. AARO reiterates it has found no evidence of extraterrestrial beings or technology to date and describes the multi-step process required to declassify UAP records.

_qa.public_headline: Oak Ridge Lab Found Alleged UAP Crash Metal Is Terrestrial
_qa.public_tldr: The All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) commissioned Oak Ridge National Laboratory to analyze a layered magnesium-zinc specimen claimed to be from a 1947 UAP crash. The lab concluded the material is terrestrial in origin and that its bismuth layers could not have functioned as a terahertz waveguide, contradicting claims of antigravity properties.

title: AAROs Supplement To ORNLs Analysis Of A Metallic Specimen
description: AARO document mirrored from aaro.mil. Original URL: https://www.aaro.mil/Portals/136/PDFs/Information%20Papers/AAROs_Supplement_to_ORNLs_Analysis_of_a_Metallic_Specimen.pdf

_qa.public_headline: Lab Tests Find Alleged Alien Crash Metal Is Ordinary Terrestrial Alloy
_qa.public_tldr: AARO and Oak Ridge National Laboratory tested a magnesium alloy specimen publicly claimed to be debris from a 1947 extraterrestrial vehicle crash. Their analysis found the material's isotopic composition is consistent with terrestrial origin, it cannot function as the terahertz waveguide claimed by proponents, and its properties match mid-20th century magnesium alloy manufacturing.

name: DOW-UAP-D017_General_Correspondence_Of_Sandia.pdf
title: DOW-UAP-D017, UAP Reported at Sandia Base, 1948-1950
description: This file contains 116 pages of documentation from the Armed Forces Special Weapons Program (AFSWP) – the direct, post-World War II successor to the Manhattan Project – and from the U.S. Air Force – relating to a series of sightings and investigations in Sandia, New Mexico, from 1948-1950. This file contains 209 sightings of “green orbs,” “discs,” and “fireballs” reported near the military base. Witnesses reported unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) maneuvering, flying out of sight, disappearing, or exploding. The documents also include the results of contemporary investigations into residual copper powder found in some areas where sightings were reported. A few of these investigations became the basis for Project Grudge, which collected reports of unidentified flying objects from various other military installations – also included in this collection.

title: CIA-UAP-D001, Intelligence Information Report, USSR, 1973
description: This document is a Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) intelligence information report (IIR) that describes human intelligence gathering activities in the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR). This report characterizes its content as informational, not as finally evaluated intelligence. In section 14 of this document, the source describes an incident occurring in summer of 1973, where he allegedly observed an airborne, luminous, bright green, unidentified object. The source described concentric circles forming around the phenomenon over a period of several minutes, before it dissipated. The source also stated that no sound attended the observation. The source offered no opinion on the nature of the phenomenon and was unable to provide further details regarding the incident.

title: ODNI-UAP-D001, USPER Narrative, Senior USIC Official
description: This document is a first-hand account written by a currently serving (May 2026) senior U.S. intelligence official. The official was part of a team investigating reports of unusual noises and sightings of unidentified anomalous phenomena in and near a sensitive U.S. military facility in late 2025. From the official’s vantage point as a helicopter passenger, the official recounts encountering unidentified “glowing orbs” both at close range and at a distance. The account describes an apparent high-speed object moving low to the ground, which appeared to split in two and accelerate away in two different directions. It also describes numerous higher-altitude “orbs,” some of which the official assessed to be in close proximity to the helicopter. This account is accompanied by infrared imagery taken during the same exercise by other federal officials from the ground, originally released on war.gov/UFO on May 8, 2026.

name: dow-uap-d20-mission-report-iraq-2023.jpg
title: DOW-UAP-D020, Mission Report, Iraq, 2023
description:
This document is a Mission Report (MISREP), a standardized reporting form the U.S. Military uses to record the circumstances surrounding its operations. U.S. military services often use MISREPs to report Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) to AARO. The GENTEXT, or “general text” section of these reports often contains important qualitative, contextual information, distinguishing it from the more quantitative, or numerical, data found elsewhere in the report.
A U.S. military operator reported observing “several bright objects maneuvering quickly” west to east northeast. The operator reported achieving a track on the UAP via an onboard targeting pod for approximately 20 seconds. The report describes that UAP then dimmed and disappeared from the targeting pod.
All descriptive and estimative language contained in this report reflects the reporter’s subjective interpretation at the time of the event. Such characterizations should not be interpreted as a conclusive indication of the presence or absence of any intrinsic object features or performance characteristics.

title: NASA-UAP-D008, Apollo 12 Medical Debriefing - Tape 12, 1969
description:
During a medical debriefing of the crew of the Apollo 12 mission, Commander Charles “Pete” Conrad, Command Module Pilot Richard “Dick” F. Gordon, and Lunar Module Pilot Alan L. Bean describe their observations of instances of light flashes or “streaks of lights.” The astronauts each reported that these experiences occurred in the dark as they tried to sleep.
The NASA medical team considered whether similar phenomena reported by Apollo 11 Lunar Module Pilot Buzz Aldrin had been attributable to exposure of the retina by cosmic rays. NASA later determined that the phenomena reported by the Apollo 12 flight crew were internal to the astronauts’ vision rather than external light sources.

_qa.public_headline: Apollo 12 Crew Reported Seeing Light Flashes in Space
_qa.public_tldr: This is an auto-transcribed audio recording of a post-mission medical debriefing in which the Apollo 12 crew described seeing flashes and streaks of light while trying to sleep in the darkened spacecraft. NASA's medical team discussed whether cosmic rays striking the retina could explain the phenomenon, noting they had photographed astronaut retinas since the Mercury programme but never found visible damage.

title: NASA-UAP-D009, Apollo 17 Audio Excerpt, December 7, 1972
description:
During the eleventh and final crewed mission in the Apollo program, Apollo 17 Commander Gene Cernan, Lunar Module Pilot Harrison Schmitt, and Command Module Pilot Ronald Evans report seeing small lights outside the Apollo spacecraft during transit to the moon. 
The crew describe bright “particles” or “fragments” as being “jagged,” “angular,” and drifting near the Apollo spacecraft and the separated Saturn S-IVB stage. The Apollo 17 crew speculate that paint chips or ice chips are likely the source of these lights and note that they “twinkle” and move away from the Saturn S-IVB stage.

_qa.public_headline: Apollo 17 Crew Reported Bright Fragments Outside Spacecraft in 1972
_qa.public_tldr: This is an auto-transcribed audio excerpt from the Apollo 17 mission on 7 December 1972, released as part of the US Department of War's PURSUE collection. During transit to the Moon, the crew observed bright, flat, flake-like fragments drifting near the spacecraft and speculated they were mundane debris — possibly paint chips or material from the Saturn rocket's S-IVB upper stage.

title: NASA-UAP-D010, Mercury Atlas 9 Audio Excerpt, May 15, 1963
description: Approximately one hour and 41 minutes into the final and longest flight of Project Mercury, Mercury-Atlas 9 mission (MA-9) Faith 7 Pilot L. Gordon Cooper Jr. notes that he sees “John’s fireflies,” referring to John Glenn’s term from the Mercury-Atlas 6 mission. NASA later determined that the “fireflies” are attributable to frozen condensation separating from the spacecraft body. The white, green-hued appearance of this phenomenon results from sunlight reflecting off frozen condensation.

_qa.public_headline: Astronaut Cooper Reported Glowing Particles During 1963 Orbital Flight
_qa.public_tldr: This is an auto-transcribed audio excerpt from NASA's Mercury-Atlas 9 mission on 15 May 1963, in which astronaut Gordon Cooper described luminous white-green particles drifting away from his spacecraft in low Earth orbit. The particles were the same 'fireflies' phenomenon first reported by John Glenn on an earlier Mercury mission.

title: NASA-UAP-D011, Mercury Atlas 9 Audio Excerpt, May 15, 1963
description: During the final and longest flight of Project Mercury, Mercury-Atlas 9 mission (MA-9) Faith 7 Pilot L. Gordon Cooper Jr. describes the brilliant blue of sunrise beneath the haze layer of the Earth’s atmosphere. As he approaches sunrise, he describes small, luminous, brilliant white particles drifting away from the spacecraft. Cooper describes observing “fireflies” after deploying beacons, which are spherical mission-related equipment with xenon strobe lights.

_qa.public_headline: Mercury Atlas 9 Audio Captures Pilot Observing Particles in Orbit
_qa.public_tldr: This is an auto-transcribed audio excerpt from the Mercury-Atlas 9 (Faith 7) spaceflight on 15 May 1963, capturing pilot-to-ground communications during orbital sunrise. The pilot describes brilliant white particles drifting from the spacecraft and luminous 'firefly'-like particles produced by thruster firing — both identified in mission documentation as equipment-related (xenon strobe beacons and thruster debris), not unexplained phenomena.

title: NASA-UAP-D012, Mercury Atlas 8 Audio Excerpt, October 3, 1962
description: During the Mercury Atlas 8 mission, Sigma 7 pilot Walter M. “Wally” Schirra Jr. describes observing “little white objects that tend to come from the capsule itself and drift off.” Schirra later also refers to those objects as “particles” and “lathe shavings.” Schirra also describes seeing a burst of light in the window, whose source he cannot identify. He speculates that his observation corresponds with the moment the sun passes below the horizon during sunset.

_qa.public_headline: Mercury Atlas 8 Pilot Reported White Objects and Light Burst in Orbit
_qa.public_tldr: This is an auto-transcribed audio excerpt from NASA's Mercury Atlas 8 (Sigma 7) mission on 3 October 1962, in which the pilot reported small white objects drifting from the capsule and an unidentified burst of light near orbital sunset. The pilot himself attributed the white objects to capsule debris, likening them to lathe shavings.

title: NASA-UAP-D013, Mercury Atlas 7, May 24, 1962
description: During the fourth crewed spaceflight and second orbital flight of Project Mercury, Mercury-Atlas 7 (MA-7), Aurora 7 pilot Scott Carpenter describes white particles in view that appear to move at “random” and “look exactly like snowflakes.” He describes these phenomena as reflective, and that some seemed to move faster than the Aurora 7 spacecraft.

_qa.public_headline: Mercury Astronaut Reported White Particles Outside Capsule in 1962
_qa.public_tldr: This is an auto-transcribed audio recording from NASA's Mercury-Atlas 7 mission on 24 May 1962, in which the pilot described white particles resembling snowflakes moving in random patterns outside the spacecraft in low Earth orbit. The particles were later widely attributed to ice crystals from the spacecraft's own systems, though this document alone contains no sensor data or formal conclusion.

title: NASA-UAP-D014, Mercury-Redstone 4, July 21, 1961
description: During the recovery of the fourth launch and second crewed spaceflight of Project Mercury, Mercury-Redstone 4 (MR-4) Liberty Bell 7, the recovery team discusses a dye pack in the water that did not activate.

description: Declassified UFO/UAP-related case files from the FBI Vault. Originals cover roughly 1947–1977, including Project Blue Book era reports, Roswell-related material, and historical sighting investigations. Scanned PDFs from the FBI public reading room.

_qa.public_headline: FBI Files Bundle Seven Unrelated Flying Disc Reports From 1948–1949
_qa.public_tldr: This section of the FBI Vault contains a grab-bag of unrelated flying saucer materials from 1948–1949, including the well-known Chiles-Whitted airline pilot sighting near Montgomery, Alabama, a cigar-shaped object seen across Virginia, a toy manufacturer's promotional letter, and Robert Ripley's debunked claim to possess a Japanese flying saucer. No cases reached a firm conclusion.

_qa.public_headline: FBI Files Show Saucer Reports, Hoaxes, and Dead Ends From 1947–1950
_qa.public_tldr: This batch of FBI records from 1947 to 1950 contains police eyewitness reports, citizen tips, an anonymous letter claiming Howard Hughes financed a secret flying craft, a filmed sighting, and a confirmed hoax — all met with form replies from Director Hoover's office. Heavy redactions and poor document quality obscure many details.

_qa.public_headline: FBI Files from 1950: Hoaxes, Radar Blips, and Jurisdictional Confusion
_qa.public_tldr: This FBI file compiles internal memos and press clippings from 1950 covering a cardboard flying saucer hoax near Elmira, NY, a dubious letter from Mexico claiming scientific study of flying discs, and a detailed but inconclusive investigation into radar detections of an object at roughly 100,000 feet over the Oak Ridge nuclear facility in Tennessee. Names of nearly all witnesses and military officers are redacted throughout.

_qa.public_headline: FBI Files Show Bureau Forwarded Citizen UFO Reports to Air Force
_qa.public_tldr: This section of the FBI's UFO files contains internal memos and letters from roughly 1947 to 1952 in which citizens reported flying saucer sightings to the Bureau. The FBI's consistent response was that the matter fell under Air Force jurisdiction, and it forwarded the reports accordingly. The documents are heavily redacted and many pages are nearly unreadable due to poor scan quality.

_qa.public_headline: FBI File Documents Discredited 1952 UFO Sighting Near Baltimore
_qa.public_tldr: This FBI file contains an Air Force investigation into a 1952 claim by Donald Stewart that a glowing disk hovered over his car south of Baltimore, killing his engine and cracking his paint. Investigators found no corroboration: Stewart's only supposed witness admitted he saw nothing, multiple acquaintances called Stewart an exaggerator, and the car had been recently repainted. The file also includes brief reports of separate sightings at the Savannah River Plant and in Ashland, Kentucky.

_qa.public_headline: Air Force Summary Flagged Unexplained Green Fireballs Near Nuclear Sites
_qa.public_tldr: This May 1950 US Air Force Office of Special Investigations report summarised 18 months of unexplained aerial phenomena — mainly green fireballs — observed near sensitive military and government installations in New Mexico. Two inter-agency conferences at Los Alamos failed to explain the sightings, and a scientific study was contracted to investigate further.

_qa.public_headline: Indiana Civil Defense Volunteer Wrote FBI About Local Flying Saucer Group in 1953
_qa.public_tldr: In January 1953, a Civil Defense volunteer in Franklin, Indiana wrote to FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover asking for clearance information on a local organisation interested in flying saucers, noting that its members also worked in Civil Defense. The letter was bundled with a personal five-year saucer study, an enthusiast newsletter, and a sighting report describing three objects over Franklin in July 1952.

_qa.public_headline: FBI Files Show 1956 UFO Sighting Report and Hoover Denial
_qa.public_tldr: This batch of FBI documents from around 1956 includes a witness interview about a silent bright light seen near Henderson, North Carolina, a high school student's letter asking the FBI about an alleged alien contact story from a popular book, and J. Edgar Hoover's flat denial that any such matter was ever reported to the Bureau. A separate Air Force counter-intelligence letter forwards a document found inside a book in Alaska.

_qa.public_headline: FBI Memos Cover a Michigan UFO Photo Inquiry and a Denver Flying Saucer Lecture
_qa.public_tldr: This FBI file contains two 1960 field office memoranda: one from Detroit about a citizen's complaint that FBI agents seized UFO photographs (which the Bureau denied), and one from Denver where an agent attended a public lecture by a self-described aviation veteran who claimed personal contact with extraterrestrials. Neither memo contains FBI conclusions or endorsements of any claims made.

_qa.public_headline: FBI File Contains 1960s UFO Believer Letters to Hoover and NASA
_qa.public_tldr: FBI Part 15 includes correspondence and newsletter material from the International Get Acquainted Program (IGAP), a UFO contactee organisation. The documents feature letters sent to FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover, Queen Juliana of the Netherlands, and NASA, along with an account of a 1967 visit to NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center where UFO films were shown to officials who were reportedly impressed but declined to make public statements.

_qa.public_headline: FBI Files Show Radar Tracked Object at 4,500 MPH in 1957
_qa.public_tldr: This is the final installment of the FBI's released UFO files, containing mostly illegible sighting report forms and a few readable internal memos. The most substantive section describes a September 1957 radar detection over the Long Island–Pennsylvania area of an object at 50,000 feet travelling up to 4,500 mph — a speed US scientists at the time called improbable for any known aircraft.

title: NASA-UAP-D008, Apollo 12 Medical Debriefing - Tape 12, 1969
description:
During a medical debriefing of the crew of the Apollo 12 mission, Commander Charles “Pete” Conrad, Command Module Pilot Richard “Dick” F. Gordon, and Lunar Module Pilot Alan L. Bean describe their observations of instances of light flashes or “streaks of lights.” The astronauts each reported that these experiences occurred in the dark as they tried to sleep.
The NASA medical team considered whether similar phenomena reported by Apollo 11 Lunar Module Pilot Buzz Aldrin had been attributable to exposure of the retina by cosmic rays. NASA later determined that the phenomena reported by the Apollo 12 flight crew were internal to the astronauts’ vision rather than external light sources.
